chunks: That was narrated - Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The broken one is carried and Tawaf is performed for him, and the one with a full stomach is thrown [with stones] and Tawaf is performed for him and prayer is performed for him.
And whoever carries a sick person and performs Tawaf with him, that Tawaf suffices for him as well. That was narrated.

key_terms.الْكَسِيرُ: The broken one (often referring to the elderly or those with mobility impairments)
key_terms.الْمَبْطُونُ: The one with a full stomach (often referring to those with digestive ailments or specific physical conditions)
key_terms.يُطَافُ بِهِ: Tawaf is performed for him (on his behalf)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for performing Tawaf and prayer on behalf of a sick person who cannot move or stand?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the flexibility in Hajj rituals for the physically incapacitated, distinguishing between those who can be carried for circumambulation and those who require stone-throwing while being carried. The hadith establishes that delegating the ritual act to another person is valid, yet performing it jointly with the patient also suffices, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of ease (*taysir*) in worship. This ruling underscores the balance between maintaining the sanctity of the rites and accommodating genuine physical hardship.
